title: Inventor G: excess closure exists only for line unions (rank ~ s/6) and log-space progressions (need logs)
question: Inventor G (ECDLP-55, factor bases with excess group closure): negative. Coordinate-defined sets (x/y windows, joint boxes, bit patterns, low Hamming weight, order statistics, arithmetic progressions in x, x*y windows) have m=3 closure ratio 1.00 +- 0.02 at 14-20 bits. Exception (m=2): y-windows and linear-form windows (unions of whole lines) have excess closure growing with p (slope 0.29 [0.27,0.32] log2 per bit, ratio 4.9 to 26 over 14-22 bits at s=2.5 p^{1/3}) because the three points of E on a line sum to O; but the relations lie on disjoint lines, relation-matrix rank only 0.17-0.19 s, so the exponent stays 1/2 (finding post hoc, in hashed PROTOCOL_ADDENDUM). Images of short vectors (aG1+bG2): ratio 52 to 520 but 99.5-100% trivial, coverage of targets collapses, membership needs a log. Local search finds high-closure sets (ratio 8-25) that are arithmetic progressions in log space (description = the logs).
rationale: Open question (1) of the round-15 checkpoint DEC; user directive to give everything.

PI derivation (unreviewed): a base that is a union of L lines has about L rational points (expected roots per line 1) and about L/6 relations (lines with 3 rational roots), so rank <= ~s/6 for any number of pencils, matching the measured 0.17-0.19 s; more relations per point require each point on many base lines, i.e. approximate closure under the group law (an approximate subgroup / small-doubling set), which in a prime-order cyclic group means log-space progressions whose membership test needs the logs. Two-pencil coupling therefore cannot reach rank s; not pursued.
next_action: Closed. Residual question: an efficiently testable small-doubling subset of E(F_p) without logs; sum-product type results for elliptic curves (literature check) are expected to rule this out.
